screens.name: Home — available and unavailable omen, Chrome/WebKit, normal/large
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–30 and 59–62 show the orb-led composition and both omen states, with supplied browser evidence confirming visibility and contrast.
findings: Strengthen the small sample question and clarify whether an unavailable omen consumed today's attempt.

screens.name: Input choice — approach and entry-choice
screens.evidence: Sheets 5 and 19 show distinct typing and speaking actions, and supplied lifecycle checks confirm the screen waits without starting recognition.
findings: Preserve the explicit, persistent choice between typing and speaking.

screens.name: Question composer — self and collapsed named person
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–7 and 47 show retained questions, recipient controls and consistent fields at both text sizes.
findings: Reduce surrounding vertical spacing at large text so the alternative speech action is easier to discover.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained viewport and long question
screens.evidence: Sheets 26–27 show internal field scrolling and a visible submit button, with supplied checks confirming exact draft retention and moving scroll cues.
findings: Make the transition from the clipped disclosure to the active question field less visually abrupt.

screens.name: Named-person editor
screens.evidence: Sheets 6–7 show the selected recipient, focused name input, privacy explanation and explicit confirmation.
findings: Tighten large-text spacing enough to bring Cancel changes closer to the confirmation action.

screens.name: Voice unavailable or denied
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–31 show an understandable microphone failure with typing and retry routes, while actual speech remains unverified.
findings: Verify the permission-recovery instructions against an actual device microphone-denial flow.

screens.name: AI consent — initial review, scrolled disclosure and declined return
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–19 show the disclosure, permission switch and retained composer, with supplied checks proving separate opt-in and send actions.
findings: Explain beside the switch that enabling permission returns to a separate Ask step, and give the bottom reassurance more breathing room.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday
screens.evidence: Sheet 32 shows optional labeled birthday fields, a focused heading and stacked large-text inputs.
findings: Reduce large-text vertical spacing so the optional Skip route requires less scrolling.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation without birthday
screens.evidence: Sheet 31 shows explicit age choices and the conservative reading-limit explanation at both sizes.
findings: Explain 'limits for ages 13–17' in terms users can understand without knowing internal reading rules.

screens.name: Age restriction — onboarding and profile
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 32–33 show a clear restriction and birthday-correction route, supported by supplied age-boundary checks.
findings: Preserve the clear reason for the restriction and the correction-only recovery route.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34 show actual-birthday guidance, labeled fields and a return to the age requirement.
findings: Compact the large-text heading region so users reach the correction fields sooner.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 3 and 34–35 show four choices, checkmarked selection and the changing Skip focus or Meet the Ball action.

screens.name: Birthday editing — populated
screens.evidence: Sheets 63–64 show editable saved values, Save, Cancel and a separate removal disclosure.
findings: Bring the large-text save and cancellation actions closer to the stacked fields through tighter spacing.

screens.name: Birthday editing — partial and impossible date
screens.evidence: Sheets 2–3 show retained invalid values and specific correction messages, with supplied alert and no-persistence checks.
findings: Associate the impossible-date message visually with the day and month fields as well as the form-level alert.

screens.name: Birth details — initial and editing
screens.evidence: Sheets 9–10 and 62–63 show optional time/city entry, disabled calculation and explicit city-selection guidance.

screens.name: Birth details — city results and no results

screens.name: Birth details — invalid time
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows the focused invalid time, allowed range and preserved selected city, with supplied browser recovery checks.

screens.name: Birth details — saved and successful retry

screens.name: Planning and prediction — error

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments; supplied runtime claims were considered but not independently rerun.
Screens with matching transitions and text-size variants are grouped; still frames establish visual consistency, not continuous motion quality.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, with null dimensions excluded.
The A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across every screen and component.
No demonstrated hard-gate failure is established: content outside a captured scroll viewport does not by itself prove an unreachable action.
Partially visible controls and clipped text at scroll boundaries merit targeted checks; supplied geometry checks do not establish effortless discovery.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native Dynamic Type, actual keyboard, speech, haptics, payment and OS-sharing behavior remain unverified.
Offline Circles does not demonstrate invitation, authentication or online recovery behavior.
Controlled fixtures, synthetic source text and legacy confidence labels do not establish production model semantics, calibrated confidence or predictive accuracy.
No representative novice study or independently observed assistive-technology session supports exemplary-use claims.
Standalone exported bitmap quality is outside the supplied UI deck; preview appearance does not establish final export fidelity.
Granted/revoked consent, memory Undo and timeout behavior have supplied runtime evidence but no complete corresponding visual state sequence in these sheets.
topFixes: Tighten large-text vertical spacing across birth forms, saved chart results, plans and history; capture the complete focused primary action above navigation.
Standardize secondary-action alignment and distinguish disclosure controls from navigation links.
Clarify the consent switch's next step and keep the closing privacy reassurance comfortably inside the scrolling content.
Strengthen normal-size forecast and share-preview text prominence without enlarging decorative elements.
Clarify unavailable-omen attempt status and explain age-based reading limits in plain language.
Verify the remaining browser friction with action/result captures before treating the supplied broad checks as evidence of effortless use.
